Question: In \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle DEF\), \(\angle A=\angle D=50^\circ\) and \(\angle B=\angle E=60^\circ\). What is the measure of \(\angle F\) in degrees?
Solution: \(\angle C=180^\circ-50^\circ-60^\circ=70^\circ\). The three pairs of corresponding angles are equal, so \(\angle F=\angle C=70^\circ\). This also shows that when two pairs of corresponding angles are equal, the third pair is equal as well, so ASA and AAS can be derived from each other.
